extraction.name: WikiText
extraction.description: A benchmark dataset for language modeling designed to evaluate how well models can exploit longer contexts and deal with more realistic vocabularies and larger corpora.
extraction.creator: Stephen Merity, Caiming Xiong, James Bradbury, Richard Socher
extraction.rai:dataCollection: The dataset was created by selecting Wikipedia articles that met the 'Good' or 'Featured' criteria and extracting their text via the Wikipedia API. The extracted text was then cleaned to remove lists and HTML bugs, mathematical formulae were replaced with tokens, and the text was normalized and tokenized.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: Raw text and Wikipedia mark-up from Wikipedia articles designated as 'Good' or 'Featured' by editors.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: Previous datasets like the Penn Treebank (PTB) are limited by having only lower case tokens, no punctuation, and a restricted 10k word vocabulary, making them unrealistic for real language use. Other existing large-scale datasets suffer from restrictive licensing or randomized sentence ordering.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: The dataset is intended to be used for language modeling, specifically to improve the handling of rare words and the learning and evaluation of long-term dependencies.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: For the Penn Treebank dataset, words were lower-cased, numbers replaced with N, newlines replaced with ⟨eos⟩, punctuation removed, and out-of-vocabulary words replaced with an ⟨unk⟩ token. For the WikiText dataset, list-heavy sections and HTML bugs were removed, mathematical formulae replaced with ⟨formula⟩ tokens, and normalization and tokenization performed using the Moses tokenizer. Words with a count below 3 were discarded and mapped to an ⟨unk⟩ token.

rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol.evidence: As part of the pre-processing performed by Mikolov et al. (2010), words were lower-cased, numbers were replaced with N, newlines were replaced with ⟨eos⟩, and all other punctuation was removed. The vocabulary is the most frequent 10k words with the rest of the tokens be-ing replaced by an ⟨unk⟩token. [...] Once extracted, speciﬁc sections which primarily featured lists were removed by default. Other minor bugs, such as sort keys and Edit buttons that leaked in from the HTML, were also removed. Mathematical formulae and LATEX code, were replaced with ⟨formula⟩tokens. Normalization and tokenization were performed using the Moses tokenizer (Koehn et al., 2007), slightly augmented to further split numbers (8,600 →8 @,@ 600) and with some additional minor ﬁxes. Following Chelba et al. (2013) a vocabulary was constructed by discarding all words with a count below 3. Words outside of the vocabulary were mapped to the ⟨unk⟩token
